wrongs.claim: Template Performance Score uses a 30-day rolling window (not a lifetime aggregate)
wrongs.correct: FUB tracks BOTH a 30-day rolling window (primary benchmark percentile score) AND an all-time lifetime aggregate in parallel — every column shows both views in real-time. The score is not exclusively 30-day; lifetime data is always present alongside it.
wrongs.evidence: The live FUB help article (https://help.followupboss.com/hc/en-us/articles/4402380231959-Text-Template-Performance-Score) states: "All columns update in real-time for both the running 30-day and all-time performance for each text template." The primary benchmark score does use a 30-day rolling window, but FUB simultaneously exposes an all-time lifetime aggregate alongside it — the spec's parenthetical "(not a lifetime aggregate)" directly contradicts the live documentation.

wrongs.claim: Spam Label Calling Protection uses the first 15 characters of the legal business name from Business Registration; it is not available for Canadian numbers.
wrongs.correct: Spam Label Calling Protection uses the first 15 characters of the legal business name from Business Registration (confirmed). For Canadian numbers: it is not available for Canadian numbers calling other Canadian numbers, but it CAN be applied when a Canadian account is calling US numbers — the spec's blanket "not available for Canadian numbers" is incorrect.
wrongs.evidence: The live article at https://help.followupboss.com/hc/en-us/articles/31510509488535-Spam-Label-Calling-Protection confirms the 15-character / Business Registration detail exactly. However, the Canadian-number restriction is stated with a material exception the spec omits: "Spam Label Calling Protection is not available on Canadian numbers. If a Canadian account is calling US numbers, Spam Label Calling Protection can be applied." The spec's flat statement "not available for Canadian numbers" contradicts this — a Canadian account calling US numbers IS eligible.

wrongs.section: §2.5 Total Annual Payment — Computed from observed values
wrongs.claim: Annual discount observed on Ryan Realty's account: $414 (gross $2,484 − net $2,070), representing approximately 2 months free
wrongs.correct: Annual net for 3 Grow-plan users at published rates: $2,088/year (3 × $58 × 12); annual savings: $396 (not $414). The "approximately 2 months free" framing is accurate FUB language, but strictly applied the actual discount is ~1.91 months (FUB rounds the per-user annual rate to $58, not the exact 10/12 × $69 = $57.50 that the spec used).
wrongs.evidence: FUB's live pricing page (https://www.followupboss.com/pricing) confirms "Get 2 Months Free" on annual billing. Grow Plan: $69/month/user monthly, $58/month/user annual. For 3 users (the only published configuration yielding the spec's $2,484 gross: 3 × $69 × 12), the published annual price is 3 × $58 × 12 = $2,088/year — not $2,070. Savings = $396, not $414. The spec's $2,070 figure was computed by applying exact 2-months-free math (10/12 × $2,484 = $2,070) rather than FUB's published per-user annual rate ($58/user, which rounds up from the strict $57.50). The help center article (https://help.followupboss.com/hc/en-us/articles/4402370662935) does use "savings of 2 months" language, so the framing is genuine FUB marketing — but the dollar amounts are $18 off.
